prompts.long_en: Liquid foundation models combine short gated convolutions with a small number of grouped-query attention layers. Because most layers are convolutions, the decode-time state is tiny: each convolution layer only needs to remember the last few tokens, while the attention layers keep a key-value cache. This makes the models attractive for on-device inference, where memory bandwidth, not compute, limits how fast tokens can be generated. In this test we feed a paragraph of a few hundred tokens so that every layer sees a realistic amount of history, and we compare every hidden state against the reference implementation.
